title: Little Office of Saint George, Martyr
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Heros Georgi maxime! Christi Ducis Commilito, Veram profuso sanguine Fidem probans martyrio;
blocks.english:
O greatest hero George,
Fellow soldier of Christ the Leader,
Proving the true faith by martyrdom
With blood poured forth;

blocks.source: Te nostrae nunc amandae Depraedicent camaenae: Qui inter aulae Regulos, Et Satrapas Caesareos,
blocks.english:
Let our beloved songs
Now proclaim thy praise,
Who among the petty kings of the court
And imperial rulers,

blocks.source: Excelsa belli Nomina, Cessi Phoebus inter sidera Prae cunctis elucebas, Virtutibus clarebas,
blocks.english:
Exalted names in war,
[The printed “Cessi” is unresolved.] Like Phoebus among the stars,
Thou didst shine before them all,
Resplendent in virtues,
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Cessi” is unresolved; the comparison with Phoebus among the stars is retained without inventing a conjunction.

blocks.source: Fac nos perpetua, Cum Patre, Genitoque, Paraclito Sanctoque, Gaudere gloria. Amen.
blocks.english:
Grant that with the Father,
The Begotten Son
And the Holy Paraclete,
We may rejoice in everlasting glory. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Martem secutus inclytum Christi pugil Georgius Ut Caesaris signiferi Exhibuit se strenuus
blocks.english:
Following glorious warfare,
George, the champion of Christ,
Showed himself valiant
As Caesar’s standard-bearer
blocks.editorialNote: “Ut Caesaris signiferi ... strenuus” has irregular syntax; the standard-bearer reading is provisional.

blocks.source: Aetate Juvenili: Secuta mox virili Pro milite nunc martyr sit, Ne dubium proinde sit,
blocks.english:
In his youthful years;
Manhood soon following,
Now let the soldier become a martyr,
That there may be no doubt

blocks.source: Sic Deo se, quae Dei sunt, Et Caesari, quae sua sunt, Dedisse: ut impleret, Quae Christus nos doceret;
blocks.english:
That thus he gave himself to God, and to God what is God’s,
And to Caesar what is his,
That he might fulfil
What Christ taught us;

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria et honore coronasti eum Domine,
blocks.english: ℣. Thou hast crowned him with glory and honour, O Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: ℟. Et constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum.
blocks.english: ℟. And hast set him over the works of Thy hands.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus qui nos beati Georgii Martyris tui meritis et intercessione laetificas, concede propitius, ut qui tua per eum beneficia poscimus, dono tuae gratiae consequamur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum etc.
blocks.english: O God, who dost gladden us by the merits and intercession of blessed George, Thy Martyr, graciously grant that we who ask Thy benefits through him may obtain them by the gift of Thy grace. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Partis trophaeis plurimis, Centumque fusis hostibus, Florebat amplis gratiis Et Caesarum favoribus,
blocks.english:
With many trophies won
And a hundred enemies put to flight,
He flourished in abundant graces
And the favour of emperors,

blocks.source: Tam stemmate excellens, Quam meritis praecellens: At Christiani nominis Haud immemor nec pectoris,
blocks.english:
Excelling as much in lineage
As surpassing in merits;
Yet forgetful neither of the Christian name
Nor of its spirit,

blocks.source: Christum colebat integre, Multatum quamvis sanguine Id praesciabat fore, Fidem probat cruore;
Laus sit perpetua Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Posuisti Domine super caput ejus
blocks.english: ℣. Thou hast set upon his head, O Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Coronam de lapide pretioso.
blocks.english: ℟. A crown of precious stone.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Presta quaesumus Omnipotens Deus, ut qui beati Georgii Martyris tui glorioso martyrio colimus, intercessione ejus in tui Nominis amore roboremur. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who venerate the glorious martyrdom of blessed George, Thy Martyr, may through his intercession be strengthened in the love of Thy Name. Through our Lord, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “glorioso martyrio colimus”; the English follows the readable sense provisionally.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Spontaneae solertia Occasio non desuit. Dum Caesaris saevitiae Pavore procul restitit,
blocks.english:
An opportunity was not lacking
For willing zeal,
When, far from fear,
He withstood Caesar’s cruelty,
blocks.editorialNote: The compressed “Spontaneae solertia” is rendered provisionally as willing zeal.

blocks.source: Idola contemnendo, Sic Caesari loquendo: Christiadum cur sanguinem Quid purpuram tam nobilem
blocks.english:
Despising idols,
And speaking thus to Caesar:
Why dost thou crave the blood of Christians?
Why such noble purple

blocks.source: Immisit ita appetis? Crudelis ita prodigis? Si sanguis est fundendus, Ab improbis petendus.
blocks.english:
[The printed “Immisit” is unresolved.] Dost thou so desire it?
Cruel one, dost thou squander it so?
If blood must be shed,
Let it be sought from the wicked.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Immisit” is unresolved. The remaining questions are translated without replacing it.

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua, Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Magna est gloria ejus in salutari tuo,
blocks.english: ℣. Great is his glory in Thy salvation,

blocks.source: ℟. Gloriam et magnum decorem impones super eum.
blocks.english: ℟. Glory and great beauty Thou shalt lay upon him.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Largire, quaesumus Omnipotens Deus, ut intercedente beato Georgio Martyre tuo, et a cunctis adversitatibus liberemur in corpore, et a pravis cogitationibus mundemur in mente. Per Dominum etc.
blocks.english: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that through the intercession of blessed George, Thy Martyr, we may be delivered in body from every adversity, and cleansed in mind from evil thoughts. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: His efferatus vocibus, Spumantis instar pelagi, Caesar jubet, Georgius Arcto mandetur carcere,
blocks.english:
Made savage by these words,
Like a foaming sea,
Caesar commands that George
Be consigned to a narrow prison,

blocks.source: Sed hem! Tyranne audi, Non potest virtus claudi: Est carcer ut palatium, Aulae sacrae compendium,
blocks.english:
But behold, tyrant, hear:
Virtue cannot be confined!
Prison is as a palace,
A compendium of the sacred court;

blocks.source: Nescit ligari funibus, Catenae sunt prae torquibus, Amantis in thesauro Plus vincula valent auro.
Laus sit perpetua, Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Justus ut palma florebit.
blocks.english: ℣. The just shall flourish like the palm tree.

blocks.source: ℟. Sicut cedrus Libani multiplicabitur.
blocks.english: ℟. Like a cedar of Lebanon he shall grow.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Infirmitatem nostram respice Omnipotens Deus; et quia pondus propriae actionis gravat, beati Georgii Martyris tui intercessio gloriosa nos protegat. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: Look upon our weakness, almighty God; and since the burden of our own deeds weighs us down, may the glorious intercession of blessed George, Thy Martyr, protect us. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Isthinc famet Georgius, Conviva coeli nobilis, Fame fruens pro dapibus, Supernis satur epulis,
blocks.english:
Here George hungers,
A noble guest of heaven,
Enjoying hunger in place of feasts,
Sated with heavenly banquets,

blocks.source: Nam qui divina noscit, Terrena non exposcit: Nunc nervis quoque vapulat Quos Miles Christi tolerat
blocks.english:
For he who knows divine things
Does not demand earthly things;
Now he is beaten also with sinew lashes,
Which the soldier of Christ endures,

blocks.source: Nervosus inter scuticaes Sartagines et ungulas; Quin saxum et molare Jam suscipit portare.
blocks.english:
Stouthearted amid scourges,
Pans and iron claws;
Nay, a stone and a millstone
He now undertakes to bear.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “scuticaes” and “saxum et molare”; scourges and the stone/millstone are provisional readings.

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Justum deduxit Dominus per vias rectas,
blocks.english: ℣. The Lord led the just through right ways.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: ℟. Et ostendit illi regnum Dei.
blocks.english: ℟. And showed him the kingdom of God.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui beatum Georgium Martyrem tuum virtute constantiae in passione roborasti: tribue nobis, quaesumus, ejus imitatione pro amore tuo prospera mundi despicere, et nulla ejus adversa formidare. Per Dominum
blocks.english: O God, who didst strengthen blessed George, Thy Martyr, with the virtue of constancy in his suffering, grant us, we beseech Thee, by imitating him, to despise the world’s prosperity for love of Thee, and to fear none of its adversities. Through our Lord

blocks.source: etc.
blocks.english: etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Ingens tunc surgit fabrica, Quae flexili vertigine Rotunda versans machina Cultris horrescit undique
blocks.english:
Then a huge contrivance rises,
Which turns in a yielding whirl,
A rounded machine
Bristling everywhere with knives,

blocks.source: Falce novaculisque Plus acribus, dirisque: Innexus huic Georgius Jam carne totus saucius
blocks.english:
With a scythe and razors
Still sharper and dreadful;
Bound to it, George,
Now wounded throughout his flesh,

blocks.source: In frusta vix non scinditur, Et tamen non offenditur; Nam Angelus curatum Mox adest vulneratum.
blocks.english:
Is all but cut to pieces,
Yet suffers no harm;
For an angel is soon present
To heal the wounded man.
blocks.editorialNote: “curatum ... vulneratum” is compressed; the healing of the wounded man is a provisional reading.

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Laetitia sempiterna super caput ejus,
blocks.english: ℣. Everlasting gladness shall be upon his head,

blocks.source: ℟. Gaudium et exultationem obtinebit.
blocks.english: ℟. He shall obtain joy and exultation.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui nos in tantis periculis constitutos pro humana scis fragilitate non posse subsistere; da nobis intercedente beato Georgio Martyre tuo salutem mentis et corporis; ut ea, quae pro peccatis nostris patimur, te adjuvante vincamus. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: O God, who knowest that we, set amid such great dangers, cannot stand firm by reason of human frailty, give us through the intercession of blessed George, Thy Martyr, health of mind and body, that with Thy help we may overcome what we suffer for our sins. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Fornax ardet calcaria, Et saeviente Mulciber Igne quaecunque obvia Depascitur ferociter,
blocks.english:
A lime furnace burns,
And raging Mulciber
Fiercely devours with fire
Whatever lies in its way,

blocks.source: Georgio illeso, Ardoris imperatos: Hinc magis Caesar aestuat Fornace quam succenderat;
blocks.english:
George being unharmed,
[The printed “Ardoris imperatos” is unresolved.]
Hence Caesar burns more fiercely
Than the furnace he had kindled;
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “Ardoris imperatos”; this clause remains unresolved.

blocks.source: Sed ut in igne fortius Fit aurum, sic Georgius Robustior procedit, Fornace dum excedit.
blocks.english:
But as gold becomes stronger in fire,
So George comes forth
More robust
When he leaves the furnace.

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua, Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Pretiosa in conspectu Domini
blocks.english: ℣. Precious in the sight of the Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: ℟. Mors Sanctorum ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. Is the death of His saints.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Preces nostras, quaesumus, Domine clementer exaudi, ut beati Georgii Martyris tui meritis adjuvemur, cujus passione laetamur. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: Mercifully hear our prayers, we beseech Thee, O Lord, that we may be helped by the merits of blessed George, Thy Martyr, in whose suffering we rejoice. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Convertere nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Demum Tyrannus impotens Nostrum jubet Georgium Post tantum, tamque insolens, Caput dare martyrium;
blocks.english:
At last the powerless tyrant commands
Our George, after such great
And extraordinary martyrdom,
To give his head;
blocks.editorialNote: The printed connection of “insolens,” “Caput” and “martyrium” is compressed; the English is provisional.

blocks.source: Quod lubens Ille praebet Christo, cui vitam debet; Quo facto muri concidunt, Idola passim corruunt,
blocks.english:
Which he gladly offers to Christ,
To whom he owes his life;
This done, the walls fall,
And idols everywhere collapse,

blocks.source: Terra connutat motibus, Orbam se quasi dotibus Georgii jam nosset, Abs quo non stare posset.
blocks.english:
The earth shakes with tremors,
As though it now knew itself bereft
Of George’s gifts,
Without whom it could not stand.

blocks.source: Laus sit perpetua Patrique, Filioque, Spiranti ab utroque Par sit et gloria.
blocks.english:
Everlasting praise be to the Father
And to the Son,
And equal glory to Him
Who proceeds from both.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis sancte Martyr Georgi.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, holy Martyr George.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Presta, quaesumus, Omnipotens Deus, ut beati Georgii Martyris tui fidem congrua devotione sequamur, qui pro ejusdem dilatione, martyrii palmam meruit obtinere. Per Dominum nostrum etc.
blocks.english: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we may follow with fitting devotion the faith of blessed George, Thy Martyr, who for its spreading merited to obtain the palm of martyrdom. Through our Lord, etc.

blocks.source: Tibi Martyr victoriam Applaudo contra Caesarem, Qui firmam per constantiam Hostem vicisti desidem;
blocks.english:
Martyr, I applaud thy victory
Against Caesar,
Who through steadfast constancy
Didst vanquish the slothful enemy;

blocks.source: Fac tecum nos certare, Hostesque superare: Fac mundum, carnem sternere, Terrena quavis spernere, Fac in adversis solidos, Pro Jesu quidquid strenuos (Quam nobis id amare Contingat) supportare.
blocks.english:
Grant that we may fight with thee
And overcome our enemies;
Grant that we may lay low the world and the flesh,
And despise all earthly things;
Grant that, steadfast in adversity,
We may valiantly bear anything for Jesus,
However bitter
It may be for us.

blocks.source: Divina gratia Patrique, Filioque, Paraclito Sanctoque Haec praestet munera.
blocks.english:
May divine grace grant these gifts,
To the Father and the Son
And the Holy Paraclete
[The printed construction is uncertain.]
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Divina gratia Patrique, Filioque, Paraclito Sanctoque Haec praestet munera” has an uncertain relationship between its subjects and datives. The readable words are retained and the construction is flagged.

blocks.source: ℣. Accipite armaturam Dei,
blocks.english: ℣. Take unto you the armour of God,

blocks.source: ℟. Ut possitis resistere in die malo.
blocks.english: ℟. That you may be able to resist in the evil day.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, pro cujus amore et fidei confessione beatus Georgius Martyr et Miles tuus invictissimus diversa vicit tormenta, et ad mortem usque certando capitalem subiit sententiam; praesta, quaesumus, ut qui ad eum in angustiis nostris fiducialiter recurrere praesumimus, intercessionis ejus auxilio a diaboli laqueis, et ab omni mentis et corporis adversitate liberemur. Qui vivis et regnas etc. Amen.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, for whose love and confession of faith blessed George, Thy Martyr and most unconquered soldier, overcame diverse torments and, contending even unto death, underwent the sentence of beheading, grant, we beseech Thee, that we who presume confidently to have recourse to him in our distress may, by the help of his intercession, be delivered from the snares of the devil and from every adversity of mind and body. Who livest and reignest, etc. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. The eight printed hours have distinct collects, all retained. The invocation and Gratulatio remain non-hour sections. Poetic and legendary events remain source statements, without replacing them from another life of the saint.
